newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN SPEAKER REPRIMANDS DEPUTY MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN SPEAKER REPRIMANDS DEPUTY MINISTER.

text.p: The Speaker of the South African parliament rapped Deputy Minister Essop Pahad over the knuckles on Tuesday for making unsubstantiated allegations against an opposition critic of Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma.

Speaker Frene Ginwala, a veteran African National Congress activist, made a statement to the National Assembly on the tone of a debate last week about the Health Ministry's Sarafina II funding debacle.
"In my opinion, several remarks made during the debate amount to unsubstantiated allegations of corruption or improper motives on the part of other members.
"They fall within the category of remarks which...must be regarded as offensive and hence unparliamentary.
"I want to issue a stern warning that...the Chair will not in future tolerate the kind of allegations and accusations that were made in the debate last week," she said.

Ginwala named Pahad, who accused Democratic Party legislator Mike Ellis of accepting favours from the pharmaceutical industry, and National Party member Willem Odendaal, who repeated old allegations of impropriety against ANC firebrands Winnie Mandela and Peter Mokaba.
Pahad was recently appointed deputy minister in the office of Thabo Mbeki, deputy president and President Nelson Mandela's heir-apparent.

The allegations were made during an emotional debate about a secret donor who, when his identity was about to be revealed, withdrew an offer to bail Zuma out of a 10.5 million rand crisis over the misuse of European Union aid funds to pay for the AIDS awareness play Sarafina II.
Pahad accused Ellis, one of Zuma's strongest critics, of representing the pharmaceutical industry which was angered by Zuma's campaign to cut the cost of medicines.

He accused Ellis of being in league with the pharmaceutical industry and said "he is speaking not on behalf of himself or his party, but on behalf of some hidden monopoly". Ellis later challenged him to repeat the claims outside parliament.
Ginwala said there were formal procedures laid down to impeach a fellow legislator on the grounds of corruption and said she would not tolerate vague allegations.

"The remarks by the honourable Dr Pahad...impute improper motives to the honourable Mr Ellis and I have noted that those remarks appear to have been carefully phrased and not made on the spur of the moment," she said.
